- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or erratic, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often fails to recognize it; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment shifts; use 14-day rolling average of history to anchor forecast, especially if sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” entries, model often underperforms; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for low sentiment bias.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores trend; add a small negative bias (e.g., -0.5% to -1.5%) to forecast.
